Retail consumers only generate cutoff demand in these backward-inducted subgames.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Under bank financing, a competitive lender approves the loan and applies the break-even interest rate r*=1/beta-1; the copycat decides entry after observing the retail product, and startup/copycat set retail prices simultaneously. Under crowdfunding, the startup chooses campaign price and the disclosed/provided quality fraction lambda; after campaign success the copycat chooses whether and what to imitate, then the firms compete simultaneously in retail prices. Consumers generate derived demand and are not strategic players in this financing-entry-price game. multistage financing and entry game simultaneous differentiated-price competition

models.name: Benchmark: Bank Financing Strategy
models.relation: This is an alternative to Innovation Against Imitation model.
models.summary: Third, we identify counterintuitive equilibrium conditions where heightened imitation efficiency paradoxically reduces both copycat profits and social welfare—challenging conventional wisdom about market competition. If ΠB c ≤0, the copycat stays out of the market, allowing the start-up to operate as a monopolist (bank financing with monopoly (BM); case BM). In this section, we perform sensitivity analysis on the optimal progressive launch strategy and associated profits to examine how crowdfunding market proportion and crowdfunding imitation efficiency influence this duopoly game.
